actibase Package

actibase is a baseline package for raw actigraphy and activity workflows. It provides readers and core preprocessing helpers that downstream packages can build on, such as step-count or summarization overlays.

Installation

You can install actibase from GitHub with:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("jhuwit/actibase")

Quick start 

library(actibase)
res = acti_standardize_data(acti_raw_data)
resampled = acti_resample(res, sample_rate = 30L)

What lives here

actibase keeps the primitives that other packages can build on:

  • accelerometer column standardization and axis reshaping, including common x/y/z, acc_*, and acceleration_* input names
  • timestamp-aware resampling to a sampling rate or requested timestamps
  • time-of-day, date, day-boundary, and interval helpers
  • sample-rate and device-range metadata lookup
  • raw-sample QC flags and CDC NHANES letter labels for comparing raw-data checks with NHANES output
  • day-inclusion summaries and basic zero handling

Device-limit helpers distinguish adjacent samples from sustained runs: acti_flag_adjacent_device_limit_samples() marks near-limit samples with a neighboring limit sample, while acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs() marks axis- and sign-specific runs meeting min_length. The older function names remain available for compatibility.

The flag functions label questionable raw samples and intervals; they do not replace vendor readers, wear/nonwear algorithms, or activity summaries. acti_flag_cdc_labels() is syntactic sugar for attaching CDC letter codes to flag columns already computed, so raw-data checks can be compared with NHANES.

Higher-level summarization, step-count mapping, and downstream analysis should live in overlay packages.

NHANES PAM flag mapping

The table maps the CDC NHANES PAM minute flags to the general-purpose sample-level or window-level helpers in actibase. The functions do not reproduce CDC’s data pipeline automatically: use the CDC thresholds and window rules when matching NHANES output. Flags with axis-specific output need by_axis = TRUE where that option is available. acti_flag_cdc_labels() can combine the resulting logical columns into CDC-style letter strings.

CDC code CDC definition (summary) actibase function and output Match notes
A–C Axis-specific spikes: adjacent-sample change ≥11 g acti_flag_spike(by_axis = TRUE): flag_spike_X/Y/Z Sample-level; set spike_size = 11 and use the appropriate sampling rate.
D–F Per-minute count of positive near-limit values, ≥690 samples acti_flag_device_limit_windows(): flag_device_max_X/Y/Z Set min_count = 690, window_seconds = 60, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6), and epsilon = 0.05.
G–I Per-minute count of negative near-limit values, ≥690 samples acti_flag_device_limit_windows(): flag_device_min_X/Y/Z Same thresholds as D–F, for negative values.
J–L Contiguous positive near-limit run, ≥160 samples acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs(): flag_contiguous_max_X/Y/Z Set min_length = 160; CDC also assigns the run to every overlapping minute.
M–O Contiguous negative near-limit run, ≥160 samples acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs(): flag_contiguous_min_X/Y/Z Set min_length = 160; CDC permits runs to cross minute boundaries.
P Contiguous impossible gravity values acti_flag_impossible(): flag_impossible Generalized thresholds are configurable; CDC uses seven samples, <0.01 g change on each axis, vector magnitude >1.25 g, excluding ±6 g values.
Q Contiguous adjacent zero values acti_flag_all_zero(): flag_all_zero Package checks all three axes. CDC documents a historical programming error that checked only X; exact reproduction of that error is not intended.
R Contiguous identical, non-zero three-axis samples acti_flag_repeated_samples(): flag_repeated_samples Configure min_length = 2, exclude_zero = TRUE, require_equal_axes = TRUE. CDC’s reported run length/minute attribution may differ.
S–U Axis-specific 1-second spike counts acti_flag_spike_second(by_axis = TRUE): flag_spike_second_X/Y/Z Set window_seconds = 1, min_spikes = 13, spike_size = 11; CDC counts qualifying local-extremum events.
V Minute before and after an invalid minute acti_flag_adjacent_invalid_periods(): flag_adjacent_invalid Caller supplies invalid periods; CDC’s hour-boundary exception requires matching group boundaries.
W–Y Axis-specific interval jumps within a second acti_flag_interval_jump(by_axis = TRUE): flag_interval_jump_X/Y/Z Set window_seconds = 1, min_repeats = 10, min_distinct = 3, min_separation = 0.5; implementation is an approximation of the CDC interval-jump rule.

Letter labels are made from columns already present in the data; the helper does not run detectors or infer missing axis-specific results:

raw <- acti_flag_spike(raw, by_axis = TRUE)
raw <- acti_flag_device_limit_windows(raw, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6),
                                      min_count = 690)
raw <- acti_flag_contiguous_device_limit_runs(raw, dynamic_range = c(-6, 6),
                                              min_length = 160)
raw <- acti_flag_cdc_labels(raw)
